In [[queueing theory]], a discipline within the mathematical [[probability theory|theory of probability]], a '''rational arrival process''' ('''RAP''') is a mathematical model for the time between job arrivals to a system. It extends the concept of a [[Markov arrival process]], allowing for dependent [[matrix-exponential distributed]] inter-arrival times.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1081/STM-120018141| title = Matrix‐Exponential Distributions: Calculus and Interpretations via Flows| journal = [[Stochastic Models]]| volume = 19| pages = 113| year = 2003| last1 = Bladt | first1 = M. | last2 = Neuts | first2 = M. F. }}</ref>

The processes were first characterised by Asmussen and Bladt<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1016/S0304-4149(99)00006-X| title = Point processes with finite-dimensional conditional probabilities| journal = [[Stochastic Processes and their Applications]]| volume = 82| pages = 127| year = 1999| last1 = Asmussen | first1 = S. R. | last2 = Bladt | first2 = M. | doi-access = free}}</ref> and are referred to as rational arrival processes because the inter-arrival times have a rational [[Laplace–Stieltjes transform]].

==Software==

* [https://win.uantwerpen.be/~vanhoudt/ Q-MAM] a [[MATLAB]] toolbox which can solve queueing systems with RAP arrivals.<ref>{{Cite book | doi = 10.4108/ICST.VALUETOOLS2008.4368| chapter = Q-MAM: A Tool for Solving Infinite Queues using Matrix-Analytic Methods| title = Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Performance Evaluation Methodologies and Tools| year = 2008| last1 = Pérez | first1 = J. F. | last2 = Van Velthoven | first2 = J. | last3 = Van Houdt | first3 = B. | isbn = 978-963-9799-31-8| url = http://www.pats.ua.ac.be/content/publications/2008/Perez_VanVelthoven_VanHoudt_QMAM.pdf}}</ref>
